title: Total different estimates
prompt: IEstimate is supplied. Finish two classes that implement it. FlatEstimate takes a number of minutes and returns it from Minutes(). ItemEstimate takes a number of items and the minutes for each, and Minutes() returns the two multiplied. Then finish Estimates.Total so it returns the Minutes() of every estimate added together, and 0 for an empty list.
hints: What does each class need to remember between its constructor and its Minutes() call?
Total does not need to know which class it has. It only needs Minutes().
Store the constructor values in properties. In Total, loop and add estimate.Minutes() to a running total.
checks: Estimates.Total(new List<IEstimate> { E(new FlatEstimate(30)), E(new ItemEstimate(4, 5)) }) == 50
checkLabels: A flat estimate of 30 must give 30.
4 items at 5 minutes each must give 20.
A flat 30 and 4 items at 5 minutes must total 50.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Adds the items and the minutes instead of multiplying.
Counts the estimates instead of adding their minutes.

feedback: Check each class on its own first, then Total. Total should call Minutes() on every estimate without asking which class it is.
